note:
The subject is a scheduled night telling a budget it reached from weather it did not (#890).

Measured: run 43154285437, the falsify night of 2026-11-12, started 04:21:45 and ended `cancelled` at 07:52:04. That is 210.3 minutes against the `timeout-minutes: 210` falsify.yml declares for itself, and its long step carried the conclusion `cancelled` rather than `failure`. The classification looked for a failing step, found none, and reported "the run's own infrastructure — a lost runner, a cancellation, an unreachable dependency".

None of those was true. The 0.16 batch had added 23 specs and 263 mutations and that night was the first to replay them: the work had outgrown its budget, which is a fact about this repository. Filing it as weather is how the one instrument that proves this repository's tests bite stopped going to the end with nobody owning it.

tools/ci/testdata/budget-night is that run's field-trimmed payload, timestamps included, and cancelled-night is the counter-witness: no timestamps, so nothing may be claimed about a budget from it.

mutations.label: the budget branch is never taken, so a job that ran its declared ceiling to the end is reported as a lost runner again. The condition is neutralised rather than removed, so every name still evaluates
the budget findings are filtered out of the body, so the report measures the ceiling and then does not say it. A verdict computed and not printed is the same silence as one never computed

the grep that reads the declared budgets loses its failure guard. This file runs under `set -euo pipefail` and grep exits 1 when it matches nothing, which is the ordinary case for a workflow declaring no timeout — drift.yml is one — so every night with nothing to report here dies instead. The same trap that killed the backlog step of drift.yml the first time it met a run: block's own -e
